concept.name: Double exponential moving average
concept.definition: Patrick Mulloy's Double Exponential Moving Average (Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, January 1994): a composite of a single and a double EMA that subtracts the extra lag of the double-smoothed series from the single-smoothed one to track price more closely.
concept.intuition: Measure how much double-smoothing lags single-smoothing, and add that gap back to the fast EMA as a correction.
concept.mechanics: EMA1 = EMA(price), EMA2 = EMA(EMA1); DEMA = 2*EMA1 - EMA2. The double-smoothed EMA2 serves only as a lag-correction term, not as the output. Default 20 periods; signals via price/line crosses or fast/slow DEMA crossovers, which occur earlier than equivalent EMA crossovers.
concept.failure_modes: Greater responsiveness means more noise and more false signals in choppy markets; long-term investors may be better served by a traditional, smoother average.
concept.misconceptions: DEMA is not simply the EMA of an EMA — that double-smoothed series alone would lag more, not less; the output is 2*EMA1 - EMA2.
concept.example: If EMA1 = 50 and EMA2 = 48, DEMA = 2*50 - 48 = 52, pulling the average above EMA1 toward current price.

citations.source: Double Exponential Moving Average (DEMA) | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
